$comment: Every Malaysian gateway bayarkit knows about. sources = official documentation and official SDK code only. Fingerprints: sources.lock.json (node tools/rujukan.mjs check).

sources.title: toyyibPay API reference

gotchas.text: A bill with no transactions answers the text `No data found!`, not `[]`: a strict JSON parser reports every unpaid bill as an error.
Callbacks arrive as `multipart/form-data`; code that only parses URL-encoded bodies sees no fields.
`billExpiryDate` is read in Malaysia time, and RM1.00 (100 sen) itself is accepted although the docs say "more than RM1.00".

gotchas.text: The checksum sorts values by field NAME and joins them with `|`; a `payment_channel` list is joined with `,` inside it.
`amount` is ringgit with two decimals ("25.00") in both the JSON body and the checksum; a callback may carry it as a number.

sources.title: Billplz API documentation
Official WooCommerce plugin: X Signature code

gotchas.text: X Signature sorts the concatenated `key+value` strings, not the keys: the docs' "sort keys" wording gives a different HMAC than the official plugin and test vectors.
gotchas.source: support.billplz.com/api X Signature steps; official WooCommerce plugin L336–341

gotchas.text: Answer the callback with HTTP 200 within 20 s or Billplz retries (up to 5 attempts over ~24 h), and callback and redirect arrive in no fixed order.
A deleted bill comes back if the customer completes a payment already in flight, so `paid=true` can arrive after DELETE.

sources.title: CHIP Collect OpenAPI (official source of truth)
CHIP docs index for LLMs

gotchas.text: Callbacks are signed in the `X-Signature` header: base64 RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 over the RAW body. `GET /public_key/` returns a JSON-quoted PEM string that must be JSON-decoded first.

CHIP's own AI skill lists fields and a status that do not exist (`failure_callback`, `cancel_callback`, status `failed`) and a wrapped payload; the OpenAPI spec has none of these. There is no `failed` status: paid means `paid`, `cleared` or `settled`.
gotchas.source: CHIP Collect OpenAPI status enum vs github.com/CHIPAsia/skill SKILL.md

gotchas.text: `success_callback` must not contain a port, not even `:443`; redirect and callback fields go at the top level of the create body (nested inside `purchase` they are ignored).

gotchas.text: API version `2026-09-30.endive` rejects `payment_method_types` on Checkout Sessions with HTTP 400. Use `allowed_payment_method_types[]` (or Dashboard payment methods), and always send a `Stripe-Version` header.
Minimum charge in MYR is RM2.00 (200 sen); FPX needs a Malaysian Stripe account with a business registration number, MYR, one-time payments only.
gotchas.source: docs.stripe.com minimum charge amounts; FPX docs

gotchas.text: Webhook signatures cover `${t}.${rawBody}` with the full `whsec_…` secret; several `v1` values can appear during secret rotation. Without the raw body, verification is impossible.

gotchas.text: senangPay merchants were migrated to the DOKU platform, so new integrations use DOKU's JSON API with an HMACSHA256= header signature; the legacy hash/form API at app.senangpay.my/payment/{merchantID} redirected to doku.com/not-found for the documented example merchant ID.

DOKU's own Python and Node.js signature samples prefix the digest line with 'Digest:' (and the Go sample appends the digest twice), while the prose and the Java/Ruby samples use the bare base64 digest: Client-Id
Request-Timestamp
Path
Digest.

Amounts are ringgit with decimals (DOKU float 100.05; legacy '25.50' with exactly two decimals that must byte-match the hashed string), not sen, except legacy tokenisation amount_paid which is in sen (200 = RM2.00); minimum payment is RM2.00.
Do not query a DOKU payment right after the redirect: Retrieve Payment/Checkout must be called at least 60 seconds after payment completion, and the {id} is your own request id, not a DOKU id.

gateways.name: NTT DATA Payment Services Malaysia (formerly iPay88) — iPay88 OPSG / ADAPTIS e-Commerce
gateways.sandbox: No public sandbox documentation. Host https://sandbox.ipay88.com.my/epayment/entry.asp answers but is undocumented in public material; the iPay88-authored spec (not officially hosted) says test against production https://payment.ipay88.com.my/epayment/entry.asp with MYR 1.00 from the Request URL registered with iPay88 support (localhost not allowed).

sources.title: iPay88 Signature Testing tool (SHA-1 / SHA-256 / HMAC-SHA512) on the live gateway host
Gateway's own HMAC-SHA512 helper used by the signature tool (CryptoJS HmacSHA512, hex output)
iPay88 SHA-256 Signature Testing tool (legacy request signature)

gotchas.text: The signature is HMAC-SHA512 (lower-case hex, 128 chars) keyed with the MerchantKey, but the MerchantKey is ALSO the first part of the hashed message (key+code+refno+amount+currency), so a 'normal' HMAC over the fields alone will never match.

Amount is posted in ringgit with two decimals (e.g. 1.00) but must be signed with '.' and ',' removed (100); the gateway's own tool removes only the FIRST '.' and FIRST ',' (JS String.replace), so amounts with two thousands separators (1,000,000.00) give a different string there than a full strip.
enquiry.asp answers with a bare text/html body, not JSON: only the exact string '00' means paid; 'Invalid parameters' and 'Record not found' are returned with HTTP 200.
gotchas.source: https://payment.ipay88.com.my/epayment/enquiry.asp (live probe 2026-10-23: empty POST -> 'Invalid parameters', unknown RefNo -> 'Record not found', both HTTP 200)

gotchas.text: The callback skey is a double MD5 over the raw POSTed strings, keyed with the SECRET key (not the verify key): md5(paydate.domain.md5(tranID.orderid.status.domain.amount.currency).appcode.secret_key).

gotchas.text: Callback URL must ACK with plain-text CBTOKEN:MPSTATOK while return/notification URLs ACK by re-POSTing all fields plus treq=1 to returnipn.php; retry count is 3 in the spec but 4 in the cheatsheet.
gotchas.source: API Spec v13.97 PDF p.52-59 (pdf 53-60); Cheatsheet README L38

gotchas.text: When 'extended vcode' is enabled in the portal the currency must be appended to the vcode hash, but the official PHP SDK never appends it, so its payment links fail with error P03.
gotchas.source: API Spec v13.97 PDF p.18-19 (pdf 19-20); SDK-Fiuu_PHP src/lib/Payment.php L36

gotchas.text: Callback currency can arrive as 'RM' instead of 'MYR' (the official plugin normalises it), so compare currencies after normalising but hash the raw value.

gateways.sandbox: https://sandbox-pgw.2c2p.com (production https://pgw.2c2p.com); public demo merchant for Malaysia JT07/MYR with a published secret key

sources.title: JWT (Generate / Decode JWT) - HS256 sample with secret key and expected token
Payment Response (Backend) - JSON {payload: JWT} POST to backendReturnUrl
Payment Token Request Parameters (amount, invoiceNo, paymentExpiry, return URLs, idempotencyID)
Sandbox Setup - base URLs, JWT auth, first API call

gotchas.text: The JWT HMAC key is the secret-key hex string used as ASCII bytes (not hex-decoded), and the official response-decoding recipe verifies a token with the JT01 key although that token is actually signed with the JT04 key, so copy-pasted sample code fails.

Only the backend notification (JSON {payload: HS256 JWT}) is signed; the frontendReturnUrl POST is unsigned base64 form data (paymentResponse=...) whose respCode 2000 only means 'do a payment inquiry', so it must never mark an order paid.

The official WooCommerce plugin (2026 build v8.1.0) does not use the documented v4 JWT API but legacy RedirectV3 with an HMAC-SHA256 concatenated-field hash and 12-digit zero-padded minor-unit amounts, while the v4 API expects decimal major units (e.g. 2500.90000), so do not port amount or signing logic from the plugin.
gotchas.source: wordpress-2c2p-build20260612.zip: 2c2p_woocommerce_new/2c2p.php L191, Includes/wc-2c2p-hash-helper.php L15-87, Includes/wc-2c2p-validation-helper.php L59-89 vs https://developer.2c2p.com/docs/api-payment-token-request-parameter.md L146

gotchas.text: Docs disagree on the API version path (4.3 in Sandbox Setup and the OpenAPI reference, 4.5 on the Payment Token and Payment Inquiry pages); both answer on sandbox, so pin one version explicitly and keep it in config.

gotchas.text: The official Node webhook sample verifies JSON.stringify(parsedBody), but the signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the RAW body bytes, so re-serialising breaks verification.

Webhooks are signed with the Dashboard webhook secret, while the checkout/callback razorpay_signature is HMAC-SHA256(order_id|payment_id) keyed with the API key secret, and order_id must be your stored one, not the posted one.
An authorized payment that is not captured within 3 days is auto-refunded, and auto-capture applies only to payments created through the Orders API.
Docs say a failed attempt needs a NEW order and that receipt must be unique, yet the official WooCommerce plugin reuses the order and repeats the receipt, so test retry behaviour yourself.
gotchas.source: https://curlec.com/docs/api/orders/create.md L19-21, L359-365 vs razorpay-woocommerce woo-razorpay.php L1188-1210, L1569

gateways.sandbox: https://api.sandbox.hit-pay.com (separate sandbox account at dashboard.sandbox.hit-pay.com, Singapore business only; own API key and salts; production https://api.hit-pay.com)

Webhooks (event webhooks + validation, Markdown export)
Online Payments guide (Markdown export)
Official PHP SDK Client.php (v1 hmac generateSignatureArray)

gotchas.text: Two signing schemes with two different salts coexist: legacy per-request `webhook` callbacks are form-encoded with an `hmac` field = HMAC-SHA256(API-key salt, sorted key+value concat without hmac), while dashboard event webhooks are JSON with a `Hitpay-Signature` header = HMAC-SHA256(per-webhook salt, raw body).
The Online Payments guide's Express sample signs JSON.stringify(req.body) instead of the raw body, which can fail on genuine webhooks; verify over the raw request bytes.
The `webhook` create parameter is called deprecated in the guide, yet the OpenAPI does not mark it and the official WooCommerce plugin still relies on it and its v1 hmac.
Sandbox accounts must be Singapore businesses and do not list FPX, DuitNow or Touch 'n Go, so Malaysian methods cannot be exercised end-to-end before production.

gotchas.text: The signed amount is the 2-decimal ringgit string with the dot removed and the leading zero kept (0.10 becomes "010", not integer sen 10).

The callback signature covers the full uppercased status text ("88 - TRANSFERRED") and the amount Gkash sends, so verify with the raw posted values and separately compare amount/currency with the order.
Query and refund responses carry no signature, so a query cannot be authenticated beyond TLS and has no paid-time field.
Docs say version "1.5.5" while the official plugin and all SDKs send "1.5.0", and the production host api.gkash.my appears only in plugin/SDK code.

gotchas.text: Webhooks carry no HMAC or signature: authentication is a static per-environment token in the x-callback-token header that must be compared with the dashboard token, so also re-check amount and status against your own record or a GET.
Amounts are in major units (RM 150 = 150, decimals allowed), not sen.
Fulfil on payment.capture rather than on the session status: a payment can still be collected after a session is cancelled or expired, and the session status will not change.
Cancel spelling differs by object: sessions and payments use CANCELED while refunds use CANCELLED, so exact string matching misses one of them.

gotchas.text: Official plugins disagree on the HashValue2 field list: eGHL_HASH and WHMCS hash ...OrderNumber+Param6+Param7, Magento 2.1.7 omits Param7, and OpenCart omits both Param6 and Param7, so a callback carrying Param7 fails verification in some plugins.
gotchas.source: bitbucket.org/eghl/eghl_hash eGHL_HASH.php line 2 vs bitbucket.org/eghl/adaptis-magento @faacfb1 zip Controller/Index/ResponseHandler.gte_m230.php:623-646 vs bitbucket.org/eghl/adaptis-opencart @38c0db3 zip catalog/controller/payment/ghl.php:206

gotchas.text: The signature is plain SHA-256 over MerchantPassword concatenated with the field values (no separator, not HMAC), and the official hash class silently returns sha256(password) alone when a mandatory field is missing.
The server callback must answer with the plain body 'OK'; the browser return URL and the server callback receive the same fields, so both must verify the hash and be idempotent.
Amount is ringgit as a string with exactly two decimals and no comma ('10.00', not sen), and the query must repeat the original Amount and CurrencyCode exactly or it will not find the transaction.
